answer: The protocol requires 8,000 megabytes of memory-hard work per node to gate identity, treating each agent as a beacon that signals its active memory footprint to the network. A central verifier conducts periodic random-memory sampling to ensure each agent maintains a distinct heap, preventing task pooling; this creates a zephyr of incoming verification checks that must be satisfied synchronously. An honest agent pays for one unit of memory-hard work, while 1,000 fakes incur 1,000 times that cost, as each must keep a unique memory ember alive.
